title: Period digest, version 1
description:
One UTC day or month: counts, exposure, distributions, cohort breakdowns, per-bucket activity and a ranked worst-call list.

The arithmetic rules here are the substance of the contract, because every one of them has a plausible wrong answer. Additive exposure and numerator/denominator fields sum across periods. `callsWithExposure` and `largestCallPeakParticipants` do not — the first must be deduplicated by call identity across the days of a month, the second is a maximum. `findingCounts[].activeAtEnd` is a boundary evaluation and is not additive either. No average of averages, medians or percentiles anywhere.

A month therefore cannot be produced from anonymous daily totals. It needs a persisted per-call contribution index to deduplicate membership, replace late outcomes and evaluate boundary state. That index is the producer's business and is never a UI payload.

id.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` for a day, `YYYY-MM` for a month, UTC. Validated against `period` below, and round-tripped through a real date by the conformance suite — `2026-02-31` matches the pattern and is not a day.

range.description: The period's own UTC bounds, half-open. Exposure is clipped to it, including for calls that started earlier.

coverage.description:
Classifies every indexed candidate call. readable + pending + failed + unknown must equal indexedCalls, which the conformance suite checks. A readable digest may itself be partial, so these counts say nothing about measurement quality.

Child periods are the month's expected and included UTC days, or a day's 24 expected hours and the hours whose input inventory was successfully evaluated. A successfully evaluated empty bucket is a verified zero; an unevaluated one must never be presented as verified absence of traffic.

callsStarted.description: Calls whose known start falls inside the period. Calls with an unknown start are not counted here and make the population partial rather than being silently omitted.

callsWithExposure.description: Each call with positive call or participant observation exposure in this period, counted once. **Not additive**: a month must deduplicate by call identity, because a call spanning three days would otherwise be counted three times.

participantSessionsStarted.description: By known membership start. A summary-only call's span may support call exposure but does not license inferred participant starts.

callExposureMs.description: Call-time, not participant-time: the two are different denominators and must never be mixed. Additive, clipped to the period.

largestCallPeakParticipants.description: The biggest single call's peak. **Not additive and not global concurrency** — a month takes the maximum of its days. The UI must label it as one call's peak, never as how many people were on the platform at once.

joins.description: Assigned to attempt start time. On reprocessing, an outcome replaces the prior result rather than adding to it. Attempts never assigned a call contribute here but not to call counts — a failed attempt must not invent a synthetic successful call.

findingCounts.description: Assigned by raise time and deduplicated by stable finding identity.

cohorts.description: Marginal totals per dimension value. Null is the unknown cohort and is never discarded. Dimensions may not be cross-combined from these margins — a combined filter requires the server's call/participant contribution query, and the UI advertises which combinations are supported.

buckets.description: A day's 24 UTC hours, or a month's UTC days. Unavailable buckets keep their own completeness so a chart can draw a gap rather than interpolate through it.

worstCalls.description: At most 20, ordered by impaired participant milliseconds descending, then impairment share descending, then call id ascending. Exposure clipped to this period, using all-category union exposure rather than a sum of categories. Calls with no assessed evidence are excluded and stay discoverable through missing-data filters. A period with no observed impairment has an empty ranking, and the UI must not substitute a ranking of its own.

callSearchResourceId.description: The paginated, filterable call list for this period. Read against this digest's revision.

cohortAggregate.title: Exposure and metrics for one dimension value
cohortAggregate.description: Exposure is assigned to the value held during each interval, so a dimension that changes mid-call splits its exposure across values rather than attributing all of it to the last one. Values of a single-valued dimension partition the eligible exposure; multi-valued SFU participation is assigned by an explicit path or ownership policy and must not duplicate overall participant time. Ambiguous intervals go to the null cohort.

value.description: Null is the unknown cohort — a real population, not an absence to drop.

digestRevision.description: The call digest generation this row was ranked from. Following the row pins that revision, so a reader never lands on figures newer than the ranking that sent it there.

assessedParticipantMs.description: The denominator for the impairment share. Zero here means no assessed evidence, which excludes the call from ranking — so a ranked row always has a positive value.
